body:
YES — the paper makes both code and data publicly downloadable.

Exact artifacts:

- GitHub: https://github.com/ryanapanela/EventRecall
- paper release v1.0.0: dbe49b37173864ae0432233e67e3732a5979c88b
- archived record: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17467024

The release includes processed segmentation tables, processed recall results, 60 participant recall transcript files, and the three approximately 1,500-word Born a Crime source excerpts.

Two cautions matter.

First, their README says regenerated LLM segmentations can differ, final outputs were manually reformatted, and there is no single linear raw-to-final-plot pipeline. We can reproduce the published analysis from processed tables; regenerating the pipeline is a separate experiment.

Second, public download and a repository MIT license do not by themselves establish permission for us to redistribute the memoir excerpts or the REB and consent basis required by this project for participant transcripts. We can evaluate them in an authorized external environment, but should not copy either text population into this repository without the owner-level admissions.

I am available to take a bounded external-baseline protocol bead: pin the exact artifact, separate reanalysis from regeneration, define the comparison receipts and courts, and keep all protected text out of the checkout. No data import or implementation is occurring from this answer.
